test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct with reference to the Supreme Court judgement in 'The State Of Tamil Nadu vs The Governor Of Tamil Nadu' on 8 April 2025?

1. The Supreme Court held that the Governor cannot withhold assent after a bill is re-passed by the legislature.

2. The Court used its powers under Article 142 to deem 10 pending Bills as having received assent.

3. The judgement laid down that the Governor may reserve a re-enacted Bill for Presidential consideration.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court ruled that the Governor does not have the discretion to withhold assent to a Bill once it is re-passed by the legislature, as per the constitutional framework.
 
• The Court exercised its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to declare 10 pending Bills as having received the Governor's assent, ensuring legislative processes are not unduly delayed.
 
• The judgment emphasized that withholding assent by the Governor without valid reasons undermines the legislative authority of the elected assembly.
 
• The decision reinforces the principle of cooperative federalism and ensures accountability of constitutional functionaries like Governors.
 
• The judgment did not include any provision for the Governor to reserve a re-enacted Bill for Presidential consideration, focusing solely on legislative assent processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 142:** It grants the Supreme Court wide discretionary powers to pass decrees or orders to ensure "complete justice" in any case, even if such actions are not explicitly provided in the statute.
 
• **Role of the Governor:** As per the Indian Constitution, the Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state and is required to act on the advice of the state council of ministers in most matters.
 
• **Legislative Process:** Once a Bill is passed by a state legislature, it is sent to the Governor for assent. The Governor can assent, withhold, return (if not a money Bill), or reserve it for Presidential consideration.
 
• **Cooperative Federalism:** This principle emphasizes the collaboration between the Union and state governments while respecting each other's jurisdictions as outlined in the Constitution.
 
• **Judicial Review:** The judiciary has the power to review the actions of constitutional authorities, including Governors, to ensure they act within their constitutional limits.
